title: Telemetry-driven per-customer policy dry-run & canary rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Add a telemetry-driven dry-run and canary rollout mechanism for per-customer/per-route batching and caching policies. This ticket implements a service that simulates policy effects (cost, latency, and quality) without applying them; surfaces confidence scores and delta estimates in Console; and provides an automated canary apply with fast rollback if monitored signals exceed configured thresholds.
motivation: We need safer automation when recommending and applying per-customer optimizations. Past manual rollouts have caused surprising cost regressions or subtle latency spikes for a small set of customers. A dry-run + canary flow lets operators evaluate real-world impact on production traffic before committing changes broadly.
scope: Implement dry-run engine, scoring model for policy impact, Console UI for dry-run reports, canary apply job with automatic rollback triggers, integration tests, and a short-term telemetry query set for signal extraction. Not in scope: global autoscaler policy changes and reusable machine-learning based optimizer (will be separate).
design_notes: Dry-run is implemented at the router level: intercept requests, simulate alternative batching/cache decisions and compute a policy footprint without mutating runtime state.

We will compute three outputs per candidate policy: (1) simulated cost_delta_per_minute, (2) latency_p99_delta_ms, (3) quality_regression_score (0-1) derived from existing eval prompts and a small holdout sample of real user prompts when available.
Policy confidence is a band expressed as ±sigma computed from bootstrap sampling over a 24-hour window of matched requests.

Allowlists inherit from customer -> route -> global ordering. Denylists are evaluated first and short-circuit simulation for blocked policies. The dry-run report will explicitly enumerate inherited allowlist/denylist reasons.

Canary apply will pick a small segment (by customer tier or explicit allowlist) and run the live policy for N minutes while the monitoring job watches three signals (cost, latency, quality) and a synthetic canary set of eval prompts.
Rollback triggers: cost_delta > +20% for 15m OR latency_p99 > +50ms for 10m OR quality_regression_score > 0.05; thresholds mirrored in the Console and adjustable per-customer tier.
All policy changes go through an audit record with a one-click revert that can be executed manually or by the automated rollback lambda.
Security: dry-run state contains sampled token prefixes; we will apply PII redaction and never persist full customer inputs. KMS-wrapped logs for any stored artifacts.
Trade-off: router-level simulation adds CPU overhead; we mitigate by sampling traffic (default 5%) and exposing a higher sampling knob for on-demand deeper analysis.
We will introduce a 'simulated_cost_breakdown' that attributes savings to batching vs caching vs quantization profiles to help roadmap decisions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): Implement dry-run engine and minimal Console report; run internally on Canary org only with sampling 1%.
Phase 2 (week 2): Expose dry-run to SRE and Solutions teams; add confidence bands and per-route breakdowns; increase sampling to 5% for targeted routes.
Phase 3 (week 3): Implement canary apply flow and automated rollback lambda; run canary for low-risk P3 customers first.
Phase 4 (week 4): Expand to medium-tier customers and gather telemetry; tune thresholds and document playbook.
Phase 5 (post-release): Add formal ML-based policy selector and auto-suggest feature (separate ticket).
telemetry_queries: cost_delta_per_minute = SUM(token_cost*count) simulated - baseline grouped by customer_id (24h)
quality_regression_score = weighted_error(eval_scores_simulated, eval_scores_baseline) using holdout prompts
policy_confidence_band = bootstrap(sampling=1000) on matched request deltas
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run reports generated in Console for a selected customer and route showing cost/latency/quality deltas and confidence bands.
Allowlist and denylist inheritance rules documented and visible in the dry-run report.
Canary apply executes on a selected customer segment; automated rollback triggers correctly when synthetic signals exceed thresholds in a staging test.
End-to-end tests covering sampling, simulation, and audit log creation included in the CI pipeline.
Security review completed and PII redaction/hardening verified by Security team.
Runbook added to the incident handbook with step-by-step rollback and postmortem checklist.
Dashboard widget with simulated vs baseline cost shows within expected noise for internal canaries (<=5% false positives during tests).
